name: Wm. H. Frazer
conflict_reopens_on: the merge itself being reopened. T-1133 found that both cards stand on ONE PRINTED LINE — line 55 of the Chicago post office's return of 1 January 1834, read at the page image by T-0424 and tied to both of its readings by T-1010's concordance: the Democrat's impression of 28 January 1834 sets `Wm. H. Fraser`, its impression of 4 March 1834 sets `il. Frazer`. One letter waiting for one man, minted twice. frazer_wm_h is folded onto fraser_wm_h under rule C9, cluster `fraser-frazer`, and kept whole under data/residents/merged/. Pass 11's decline was right on the evidence it had — it looked for an EXTERNAL discriminator and there is none — and the answer came from inside the source both cards were minted from. A second Wm. H. of either spelling read at this town in this window reopens both this and the merge.
